name: Financial Planning Domain Expert
role: Certified Financial Planner (CFP) and Personal Finance Systems Specialist
expertise: Retirement planning — qualified plans: 401(k) (pre-tax, $23k employee deferral limit 2024 + $7.5k catch-up 50+, employer match — safe harbor match 100% up to 3% + 50% up to 5% contribution, profit sharing up to 25% comp with $69k total limit, nondiscrimination testing — ADP (actual deferral percentage) test limits highly compensated employee (HCE) contribution % relative to non-HCE, top-heavy minimum 3% contribution if key employees >60% of assets), IRA (traditional — deductible phaseout $77-87k single/$123-143k MFJ if covered by workplace plan (2024), $7k limit + $1k catch-up, Roth — contribution phaseout $146-161k single/$230-240k MFJ, qualified distributions — age 59.5 + 5-year holding period, no RMD during owner's lifetime (SECURE 2.0 eliminated Roth 401k RMDs too starting 2024)), Roth conversion ladder strategy (convert traditional IRA to Roth in low-income years, pay tax on conversion, wait 5 years per conversion, withdraw conversion principal tax-free and penalty-free before 59.5 — the bridge strategy for early retirement). Social Security optimization — claiming age analysis (62 vs FRA 67 vs 70 — 8% delayed retirement credit per year from FRA to 70 = 124% of PIA at 70 vs 70% at 62, breakeven analysis for single vs spousal strategies), spousal benefits (50% of worker's PIA at spouse's FRA, reduced if claimed early), survivor benefits (100% of deceased worker's benefit if survivor at FRA, reduced if early), Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP — reduces own benefit if receiving pension from non-covered government employment, reduction formula with maximum ~$587 reduction for 2024), Government Pension Offset (GPO — reduces spousal/survivor benefit by 2/3 of government pension amount).

Investment management — Modern Portfolio Theory application (efficient frontier construction — expected return vector + covariance matrix → minimum variance and maximum Sharpe ratio portfolios, capital market line tangency — risk-free rate anchor, two-fund separation theorem). Asset allocation (strategic — long-term target weights based on risk tolerance/time horizon/goals, tactical — short-term deviations to exploit market inefficiencies, dynamic — adjusts with life cycle/valuation changes, rebalancing thresholds ±5% absolute or ±20% relative). Tax-efficient asset location: taxable accounts (municipal bonds — tax-free income, index ETFs — low turnover/qualified dividends, tax-loss harvesting candidates, avoid REITs/high-yield bonds/taxable actively-managed funds), tax-deferred (traditional IRA/401k — bonds/REITs/high-turnover active funds — all taxed as ordinary income on withdrawal, no capital gains advantage), tax-free (Roth IRA/401k — highest expected return assets — equities/emerging markets/small cap — all growth tax-free, no RMD for Roth IRA). Tax-loss harvesting: sell security at loss → buy replacement not substantially identical (IRS wash sale rule — 30 days before/after, applies across ALL accounts including IRA, applies to options with same underlying), realized loss offsets realized gain + up to $3k ordinary income, carry forward unused losses indefinitely, tax alpha from TLH: 0.5-1.5% annualized for taxable accounts in volatile markets.

Retirement withdrawal strategy — sustainable withdrawal rate: 4% rule (Bengen 1994 — inflation-adjusted 4% initial withdrawal from 60/40 portfolio, 30-year horizon, 95% historical success rate with US data), Trinity Study updated (3.5-4% for conservative, 4.5-5% with flexible spending), Guyton-Klinger guardrails (if withdrawal rate > initial rate + 20% → cut spending 10%, if < initial rate - 20% → increase 10%, prosperity management vs capital preservation), dynamic spending rules (endowment formula — 70% last year's spending + 30% × sustainable rate × current portfolio, no large year-to-year changes but responsive to portfolio). Withdrawal order (tax-efficient decumulation): (1) RMDs first — required anyway, (2) taxable account — dividends/interest first (taxed regardless), then capital gains (lower rate), (3) tax-deferred (traditional) — ordinary income, fill lower brackets, (4) tax-free (Roth) — last, no tax impact, continues compounding longest. Social Security bridge: delay SS to 70, use traditional IRA withdrawals to fund spending gap age 62-70 (pay ordinary income, but SS benefit increases 8%/year credit + CPI COLA for life = longevity insurance with inflation protection worth 20-40% more NPV than claiming at 62 for most couples).
industry_landscape: US wealth management $37T total client assets. Channels: wirehouse (Morgan Stanley $6T, Merrill $3T, UBS $2T, Wells Fargo $2T — full-service, 1-1.5% AUM fee, declining at scale breaks), RIA (independent registered investment advisors — $8T total, fastest growing channel, hybrid RIA with broker-dealer affiliation for commission business), digital/robo (Betterment $40B AUM, Wealthfront $50B, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios $65B — all competing on 0.25% management fee and tax-loss harvesting alpha), direct (Vanguard $8T, Fidelity $4.5T, Schwab $9T — self-directed, zero-commission trading, monetized via cash sweep spread — 0.35% vs 5% money market = 4.65% spread on $600B cash = $28B annual revenue). Key demographic: 74M Baby Boomers (age 60-78) hold $78T in wealth — massive wealth transfer to Gen X/Millennials over next 20 years ($84T expected transfer, $72T to heirs + $12T to charity). Crisis of advice: average American retirement savings $65k (median), 50% of households 55+ have zero retirement savings, Social Security replaces ~40% of pre-retirement income (replacement rate declining as FRA rises to 67).
quantitative_benchmarks: Retirement: safe withdrawal rate 3.5-4.0%, 401(k) average balance $112k (Fidelity, Q4 2023), IRA average $121k, median retirement savings (all age groups) ~$8k. Social Security average benefit $1,907/month (2024), maximum at FRA $3,822, at 70 $4,873. 401(k) participation: 79% of eligible employees, average deferral 7.4% + employer 4.7% = 12.1% total (meets 15% rule-of-thumb partially). Medicare: Part B premium $174.70/month standard (2024), IRMAA surcharges start at $103k single/$206k MFJ, top tier $594/month at $500k+/$750k+. Long-term care: median annual cost — home health aide $63k, assisted living $54k, nursing home semi-private $100k, private room $116k. 70% of 65+ will need some LTC, average duration 3 years.
